_confirmMechanismNote: HOW A CONFIRMATION CLICK IS OBSERVED, and the single switch for the cutover. `double_opt_in`: the Klaviyo list is double opt-in, Klaviyo only adds a profile once the opt-in link is clicked, so membership of the subscribed set IS the confirmation. `flow_link`: the list is SINGLE opt-in, entrants are subscribed on form submit, and a branded flow email carries the confirmation link (update_property_link writes gv_confirmed). Under flow_link, subscription proves NOTHING — reading it as confirmation pays the +2 to every submitter and inflates every §5 referral rung with it. lib/giveaway/reconcile.js resolveMechanism() is the only reader; an unrecognised value throws rather than defaulting, because the two branches disagree about every entrant on the list at once. FLIPPING THIS IS HALF THE CUTOVER — the Klaviyo list opt-in process must be changed in the UI in the same maintenance window, and in this order: set the list to single opt-in FIRST, then flip this key. The reverse order leaves a window where entrants are on a double-opt-in list while the code has stopped believing subscription means anything, which stalls every +2 until the flip completes. See docs/giveaway-confirm-cutover.md.
_drawPoolNote: OPERATOR DETERMINATION 2026-08-22, made because the published rules contradict themselves and the draw is not built yet. §4 and §5 grant one base entry for submitting the form ('Base entry — submitting the entry form: 1 entry'), and §8 draws 'from all eligible entries received during the Entry Period'. But §12 says 'Sponsor will use a snapshot of confirmed entrants taken at the close of the Entry Period to conduct the drawing' — which, read literally, excludes everyone who never clicked the opt-in link. Both cannot operate. The determination is that an UNCONFIRMED entrant IS in the draw, holding whatever entries §5 grants them (base 1, plus any referral bonus §5 pays onto their entry). Reasons: §4/§5 are the sections that tell an entrant what they get and they promise it explicitly; ambiguity in a consumer promotion is construed against the drafter; and excluding people who were told they had an entry is the reading most likely to draw a complaint. §12's heading is 'Unsubscribing Does Not Forfeit Your Entry' — its subject is unsubscribers, and 'confirmed entrants' there describes the common case rather than defining an exclusion. Scale when decided: 77 confirmed holding 302 entries, 206 unconfirmed holding 1 each — unconfirmed would be ~40% of a 508-entry pool, so this is not a rounding decision. SEPARATE AND UNAFFECTED: §6's referral PRIZE still requires the named referrer to be 'themselves a confirmed entrant', which is an explicit condition with no counterpart contradiction — an unconfirmed referrer never wins the second prize. Whoever builds the draw must honour this flag; do not re-derive the pool from the Klaviyo list, which only ever contains confirmed entrants. See docs/giveaway-referral-lessons.md.
_datesNote: PACIFIC TIME (-07:00 = PDT, which is what August and September are on) and the single source of truth for timing. The deadline campaigns (05-reminder, 06-final-call) are computed from entryClosesAt by lib/giveaway/nurture-schedule.js, and close-entry-period.mjs disables the nurture flow the morning after it. The same dates appear in prose in data/giveaway/official-rules.html and in the 06-final-call preheader — change all three together. Entry OPEN date moved 2026-08-14: Aug 15 -> Aug 18 to match the ad launch. TIMEZONE moved 2026-08-20: the config stamped -06:00 and called it 'store-local' while the published rules said 'CT' (-05:00 in September), so the two named closing instants an hour apart; the operator's decision is that the giveaway runs on PACIFIC, so BOTH were wrong and both were corrected. Calendar dates did not move — entries still close September 14, 2026 and the draw is still September 16, 2026 — and the deadline campaign sendAt values below are unchanged, because campaignSchedule() does its arithmetic on the literal YYYY-MM-DD and never on the offset. If you change the offset again, re-check the server cron for close-entry-period.mjs: it is a UTC-clock cron and does NOT follow this field.
_metaPixelNote: Real Skin Care pixel, installed via the Shopify Facebook & Instagram sales channel with Maximum data sharing (Pixel + advanced matching + Conversions API). Asserted by scripts/giveaway/verify-launch.mjs.
_provisionalCostPerEntryNote: A PLACEHOLDER, to be replaced by measurement — not a finding. The spend gate compares cost per entry against what a NEW entrant is measurably worth, but no entrant is 30 days old until mid-September, so without this the gate can only say 'not measurable yet' for the whole entry window while $30/day goes out. $2.50 is the figure the adopted paid-acquisition tactics already model against ($30/day ≈ 84 entries/week, which is what puts one consolidated ad set over Meta's ~50-conversion learning threshold); it is chosen for consistency with that arithmetic, not derived from RSC data. Sanity check on how aggressive it is: at $2.50/entry, breaking even on the FIRST purchase needs roughly an 8% entrant-to-purchase rate against the $50.46 trailing-90d AOV at ~60% gross margin. That is a high bar for a giveaway list, so expect the payoff to come from repeat purchase and LTV rather than first order — and expect to lower this number once real data lands. evaluateSpendGate uses measured value the moment one 30-day window closes and ignores this entirely from then on; it labels every verdict built on this number 'provisional' in the report line.
_killThresholdNote: OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-22, pre-committed BEFORE the data arrives so the call is made against a stated condition rather than against how the campaign feels on a given morning. If fewer than 1.5% of NEW confirmed entrants place an order within 30 days of entering, the giveaway is buying sweepstakes entrants rather than customers and the campaign stops. Where 1.5% comes from: at the cost per confirmed entrant the campaign was running at when this was set (~$0.90, falling), one $50.46 order — the trailing-90d AOV — pays for roughly 56 confirmed entrants, so ~1.8% breaks even on REVENUE and 1.5% is the round number just under it. It is deliberately a revenue-breakeven floor, not a margin-breakeven one (~3.7% at 60% gross margin): a first order from a new customer is an acquisition, and the payoff is meant to come from repeat purchase, so requiring the first order to cover margin too would kill a campaign that is working as intended. NEW SEGMENT ONLY — an existing customer who enters and buys would have repurchased anyway at the ~18-22.5% baseline, so blending them measures retention and calls it acquisition. lib/giveaway/paid-readout.js refuses to return a kill verdict on fewer than 100 matured entrants, because at a 1.5% floor a smaller sample cannot tell 'does not convert' from 'has not converted yet'. Revisit once one 30-day window closes (mid-September 2026) and real entry->purchase data replaces the arithmetic above.
_metaCampaignNote: Soap Giveaway 2026-09 | Leads | US — objective OUTCOME_LEADS. Spend is read from this campaign by lib/giveaway/meta-spend.js for the daily spend gate. Recorded explicitly rather than discovered by name each run: four ad accounts exist on this token and name-matching would silently pick the wrong one if the campaign is ever renamed or duplicated.
